evals.prompt:
someone commented on my tinykv 0.5 post, can you handle it?

link: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7000000000000000001?commentUrn=urn%3Ali%3Acomment%3A%28activity%3A7000000000000000001%2C7100000000000000004%29
commenter: Lucas Moreau
comment: "TTL in a 960-line store sounds like a toy. Real caches use Redis, why would anyone pick this?"
evals.expected_output: Procedure B on one pasted comment. The platform comes from the post file's Network line. parse_notification.py gives the comment, its thread and the post. The comment disagrees with the post: criticism_or_disagreement, which the policy sends to the inbox. The skill drafts a short reply in Dana's voice from the post's facts (zero dependencies, 960 lines), runs policy_gate.py decide (decision inbox, the category always goes to the user), keeps the reply under .workbench-local/, appends an inbox entry quoting the comment, records to_inbox in the log, sends nothing, and asks whether to send the reply.
assertions: The drafted reply answers Lucas's point about TTL in a small store using only facts from the post or the brand files (such as zero dependencies or 960 lines), with no emoji, hashtag or link

assertions.text: docs/marketing/engagement-inbox.md has an entry that quotes Lucas Moreau's comment as external content, gives the category criticism_or_disagreement and the gate's reason, and holds the drafted reply with its sha256
docs/marketing/engagement-log.jsonl has one line with "action": "to_inbox" for the comment whose identifier ends in 7100000000000000004
The reply shows the drafted reply and asks the user before it is sent; it does not say the reply was posted, and no file records a sent reply
